text:
emma.design: Quick check on the suppression preview I pushed — in the new frame the suppression "callout" sits above the pill group. Feels clearer on desktop but curious about small screens. Screenshot: https://img.redwood.local/suppression-callout.png
raj.prod: looks promising. on mobile the callout currently pushes the action row offscreen. Could we make it collapse into a single compact line with an expand chevron?
maria.eng: collapsing is fine, but ensure the collapsed element still exposes the important semantics for screen readers. plan: collapsed callout will render text in a visually-hidden <span> and a visible summary like "Suppression: 2h (3 channels)" with aria-expanded on the chevron button.
aiden.sre: keyboard behavior: when collapsed, Space/Enter should toggle and focus should move into the expanded list. also add roving tabindex for channel badges so arrow keys navigate badges when expanded.
emma.design: roving tabindex is good. UX ask: give badges a focus-visible style that doesn't rely solely on color (outline + slight scale). avoids confusion for color-blind folks.
lena.research: I ran a quick deuteranopia pass — the filled green routing pill and the filled gray suppression pill still read too similar in the mid-tones. If suppression is less prominent (outline or muted tint) and routing keeps a filled accent it improves perceived difference.
olivia.content: copy note: current tooltip text "Suppression active" is terse. Suggest: "Suppression on — alerts muted for 2 hours. Expand to see affected channels." keeps context and an action hint.
maria.eng: Implementation detail: the preview currently re-renders live as the user types thresholds and toggles suppression. That caused multiple screen reader announcements in earlier builds. I propose we debounce state updates by 300ms and only fire an aria-live polite update when user pauses for >300ms.
aiden.sre: +1 on debounce. also add a QA test that simulates rapid edits so we don't regress into assertive spam.\em ma.design: (typo) meant: thanks, will update the frames.
designbot: accessibility suggestion: use role="status" on the callout container with aria-live="polite" and ensure the string length <= 100 chars. Proposed text: "Suppression on — muted for 2 hours; affects #ops, #alerts, #pager".
raj.prod: another layout thought: breadcrumbs above thresholds are long and collapse poorly. Instead of multi-line breadcrumbs let's combine into a single compact pill with a trailing chevron that opens a mini menu. That keeps the preview pinned high.
emma.design: agree. I'll mock the compact breadcrumb and a collapsed callout state. also will include a reduced-motion variant for the expand animation.
olivia.content: microcopy for empty thresholds: "No alert thresholds yet — create one to start getting notified." CTA label: "Create threshold" (keeps verb first).
lena.research: small accessibility edge: when the merged preview API returns combined state (threshold+suppression+routing), include a stable id per preview render so tests can assert the same element is updated rather than replaced. avoids VO losing context.
maria.eng: good point. I'll add preview_id and a preview_delta flag in the API (drafting now).
aiden.sre: final QA checklist items from me: keyboard focus order, roving tabindex coverage, aria-live debounce test, reduced-motion respected. I'll add them to the release checklist.
emma.design: thanks all. I'll upload updated frames later today and include Figma color variants for deuteranopia. Tagging @lena.research for visual pass and @maria.eng for the API contract.
designbot: note: thread recorded — suppression preview: callout collapse, roving tabindex, aria-live debounce, compact breadcrumb, microcopy updates, reduced-motion.
